meta.disclaimer: Guidance, not regulated financial or legal advice. Amounts are from gov.uk on last_checked; the agent must always show source_url and say 'check the official page before you rely on this'.

engine_contract.how_it_works: For each rule: evaluate `requires` (all must pass) and `excludes` (any passing = not_eligible). If a referenced fact is missing from the profile, return need_info with missing_facts = those fact keys. The LLM ONLY asks the survey_question of the missing facts and explains the result; it never decides eligibility itself.
engine_contract.ethics_guardrail: Facts with sensitivity 'special_category' (ethnicity, religion, health detail, sexual_orientation) are NEVER used in state-benefit rules. They may only be used by rules with category 'opt_in_opportunity', and only if consent.opportunities_matching is true.

dob.why_we_ask: Many benefits depend on age, including pension-age help.

nation.survey_question: Which part of the UK do you live in?
nation.why_we_ask: Some schemes only exist in some nations.

postcode.why_we_ask: To find your council's local help schemes.

has_partner_living_with.survey_question: Do you live with a partner?
has_partner_living_with.why_we_ask: Universal Credit and Pension Credit look at the whole household.

partner_dob.survey_question: What's your partner's date of birth?
partner_dob.why_we_ask: Affects your Universal Credit standard amount.

relationship_status.why_we_ask: Separated or widowed people can be entitled to extra help.

children.survey_question: Do you have any children who live with you? What are their dates of birth?
children.why_we_ask: Child Benefit, Universal Credit child amounts, school meals and childcare help all depend on this.

pregnant_weeks.survey_question: Are you or your partner pregnant? How many weeks?
pregnant_weeks.why_we_ask: Healthy Start can help from 10 weeks of pregnancy.

housing_tenure.survey_question: Do you rent, own, or live with family?
housing_tenure.why_we_ask: Help with housing costs and how much you can earn before Universal Credit drops.

monthly_rent.survey_question: How much is your rent each month?

pays_council_tax.survey_question: Is your name on the council tax bill?

adults_in_home_not_disregarded.survey_question: Apart from you, how many adults aged 18+ live with you who aren't full-time students or carers?
adults_in_home_not_disregarded.why_we_ask: If it's zero, you get 25% off council tax.

name_on_electricity_bill.survey_question: Is your name (or your partner's) on the electricity bill?
name_on_electricity_bill.why_we_ask: Needed for the £150 Warm Home Discount.

employment_status.survey_question: Are you working at the moment?

monthly_take_home_pay.survey_question: Roughly how much do you take home from work each month?
monthly_take_home_pay.why_we_ask: Universal Credit goes down 55p for each £1 earned above your allowance.

partner_monthly_take_home_pay.survey_question: And your partner's monthly take-home pay?
partner_monthly_take_home_pay.why_we_ask: Household income matters for Universal Credit.

annual_adjusted_net_income.survey_question: What's your yearly income before tax?
annual_adjusted_net_income.why_we_ask: Child Benefit is taxed back above £60,000.

savings_total.survey_question: Roughly how much do you and your partner have in savings and investments?
savings_total.why_we_ask: Universal Credit stops above £16,000 and is reduced above £6,000.

benefits_received.survey_question: Which benefits do you get now, if any?
benefits_received.why_we_ask: So we don't suggest something you already get, and because some benefits unlock others.

health_condition_affects_work.survey_question: Do you have a health condition or disability that makes daily life or work harder?
health_condition_affects_work.why_we_ask: You may be able to get PIP or extra Universal Credit. You can skip this.

needs_help_daily_living.survey_question: Do you need help with things like washing, cooking, dressing or managing medicines?
needs_help_daily_living.why_we_ask: This is what PIP looks at.

needs_help_getting_around.survey_question: Is it hard for you to plan a journey or move around?

cares_hours_per_week.survey_question: Do you look after someone who's ill or disabled? About how many hours a week?
cares_hours_per_week.why_we_ask: Carer's Allowance needs 35+ hours a week.

cared_for_gets_qualifying_benefit.survey_question: Does the person you look after get PIP daily living, Attendance Allowance, or the middle/high care rate of DLA?

weekly_earnings_after_deductions.survey_question: How much do you earn a week after tax and National Insurance?
weekly_earnings_after_deductions.why_we_ask: Carer's Allowance limit is £204 a week.

immigration_status.survey_question: Do you have British citizenship or settled status? You can skip this.
immigration_status.why_we_ask: Some help depends on immigration status. We will never share this.

is_veteran.survey_question: Have you served in the armed forces?

is_care_leaver.survey_question: Were you in care as a child?
is_care_leaver.why_we_ask: Many councils give care leavers council tax help and grants.

ethnicity.survey_question: Optional: how would you describe your ethnic background? This is only used to find opt-in scholarships, grants or mentoring aimed at under-represented groups. It never affects any benefit decision.
ethnicity.why_we_ask: Some charities and universities run schemes for under-represented groups.

preferred_language.survey_question: Which language would you like me to speak?
preferred_language.why_we_ask: So I can talk to you in your language.

accessibility_needs.survey_question: Would it help if I read everything out loud or used simpler words?
accessibility_needs.why_we_ask: So the app works the way you need.

derived_facts.reached_state_pension_age: age >= 66 (APPROX: SPA is rising to 67 between 2026 and 2028; real build should use gov.uk/state-pension-age)
derived_facts.child_benefit_eligible_children: count(children age < 16, or age < 20 and in_approved_education)

rules.title: Universal Credit
rules.summary: Monthly payment to help with living costs if you're on a low income or out of work.

work_allowance.only_if: responsible for a child OR health condition affecting work

value.taper: Payment drops 55p for every £1 earned above the work allowance

rules.estimate_formula: standard_allowance + child_elements + childcare + housing - max(0, household_monthly_take_home - work_allowance) * 0.55 - savings_deduction
how_to_claim: Create an account at gov.uk/apply-universal-credit
Have ID, bank details, rent agreement and payslips ready
Book and attend the interview at the Jobcentre

not_eligible_explanations.age: Universal Credit is for people aged 18 or over (with some exceptions at 16-17).
not_eligible_explanations.reached_state_pension_age: You've reached State Pension age, so Pension Credit is the right benefit to look at instead.
not_eligible_explanations.savings_total: Universal Credit isn't available if your household has more than £16,000 in savings.
not_eligible_explanations.immigration_status: Your current immigration status means you can't claim public funds. Please speak to a free immigration adviser or Citizens Advice.

rules.title: Universal Credit child amount (every child, no two-child limit)
rules.summary: Extra Universal Credit for each child. Since 6 April 2026 the two-child limit is gone: you get it for every child.

news_item.headline: Two-child limit has ended
news_item.body: From 6 April 2026, Universal Credit pays the child amount for every child, not just the first two. Existing claims should update automatically; if yours hasn't, report a change in your journal.
news_item.check_transactions: Compare UC payment amount before vs after April 2026; if it did not rise by roughly £303.94 per extra child, flag 'payment may be wrong'.

how_to_claim: Should be automatic from April 2026
If not, write in your Universal Credit journal: 'Please apply the child element for all my children following removal of the two-child limit'

not_eligible_explanations.benefits_received: This extra amount is part of Universal Credit, so you'd need to claim Universal Credit first.

rules.title: Universal Credit childcare costs
rules.summary: Universal Credit can pay back up to 85% of childcare costs if you work.
how_to_claim: Report childcare costs in your Universal Credit journal
Upload the childcare receipt or invoice

not_eligible_explanations.employment_status: Childcare help in Universal Credit is for people in paid work (or starting a job soon).

rules.title: Child Benefit
rules.summary: Weekly payment for anyone responsible for a child under 16 (or under 20 in approved education).

value.high_income_charge: If either parent's income is over £60,000 some is taxed back; over £80,000 it is all taxed back. Still worth claiming for National Insurance credits.

how_to_claim: Claim online at gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim
Need the child's birth certificate details

not_eligible_explanations.child_benefit_eligible_children: Child Benefit is for children under 16, or under 20 if they're in approved education or training.

rules.title: Pension Credit
rules.summary: Tops up weekly income for people over State Pension age. Also unlocks other help.

value.savings_rule: Savings up to £10,000 ignored; each £500 above counts as £1/week income

how_to_claim: Apply online at gov.uk/pension-credit/how-to-claim or call the Pension Credit claim line

not_eligible_explanations.reached_state_pension_age: Pension Credit is only for people who've reached State Pension age.

rules.title: Personal Independence Payment (PIP)
rules.summary: Weekly payment for extra costs of a long-term health condition or disability. Not affected by income or savings.
how_to_claim: Call the PIP new claims line
You'll get a 'How your disability affects you' form
Usually an assessment follows
rules.refer_out: PIP decisions are made by assessment. For help with the form, contact Citizens Advice or a local disability advice service.

not_eligible_explanations.reached_state_pension_age: PIP is for under State Pension age; Attendance Allowance is the equivalent after that.

rules.title: Carer's Allowance
rules.summary: Weekly payment if you care for someone 35+ hours a week.

value.also: If on Universal Credit, you may also get the carer element: £209.34/month

how_to_claim: Apply online at gov.uk/carers-allowance/how-to-claim
rules.warning: Carer's Allowance can reduce the cared-for person's benefits. Agent must say this before proposing a claim.

not_eligible_explanations.cares_hours_per_week: Carer's Allowance needs at least 35 hours of caring a week.
not_eligible_explanations.cared_for_gets_qualifying_benefit: The person you care for needs to get a qualifying benefit like PIP daily living or Attendance Allowance.
not_eligible_explanations.weekly_earnings_after_deductions: Carer's Allowance has an earnings limit of £204 a week after tax and expenses.
not_eligible_explanations.employment_status: You can't get Carer's Allowance while in full-time education.

rules.title: Council Tax single person discount (25%)
rules.summary: 25% off council tax if no other non-disregarded adult lives with you.

value.estimate_from_transactions: 25% of the monthly council tax direct debit

how_to_claim: Apply on your council's website
rules.transaction_signal: Council tax payments are steady AND profile says lives alone AND no discount visible (amount unchanged) → suggest.

not_eligible_explanations.adults_in_home_not_disregarded: The discount is only for homes where you're the only adult who counts. Students, under-18s and live-in carers don't count.

rules.title: Council Tax Reduction
rules.summary: Each council runs its own scheme to cut council tax for people on low incomes or benefits.

value.note: Amount depends on your council's scheme. The £1,500 income trigger is OUR heuristic, not a gov.uk rule.

how_to_claim: Apply on your council's website (find it from your postcode)

rules.title: Warm Home Discount (£150)
rules.summary: £150 off your electricity bill for winter 2026-27. Usually automatic.
how_to_claim: Usually automatic
If you get a letter asking for more info, call the helpline by 26 February 2027
rules.transaction_signal: If eligible and no £150 credit seen on the energy supplier account by Feb 2027 → remind user to call helpline.

not_eligible_explanations.benefits_received: Warm Home Discount needs one of: Universal Credit, Housing Benefit, income-related ESA or Pension Credit on 23 August 2026.
not_eligible_explanations.name_on_electricity_bill: Your name (or your partner's) needs to be on the electricity bill.

rules.title: Free school meals
rules.summary: From September 2026, every child in a Universal Credit family in England gets free school meals, whatever your income.

value.estimate_note: OUR rough estimate (~£2.60 x 190 days); not a gov.uk figure

news_item.headline: Free school meals now for all Universal Credit families
news_item.body: From September 2026, the £7,400 income limit is gone. If you get Universal Credit, your school-age children can get free school meals. You still need to apply through your council.
news_item.check_transactions: Recurring payments to a school catering provider (e.g. ParentPay) after Sept 2026 → user is paying for meals they may get free.

how_to_claim: Apply through your local council website

rules.title: Healthy Start card
rules.summary: Money on a card every 4 weeks for milk, fruit, veg and formula if pregnant (10+ weeks) or with a child under 4.

value.note: Weekly amount NOT confirmed on healthystart.nhs.uk during research; check 'Your payments' page before demo

how_to_claim: Apply at healthystart.nhs.uk/how-to-apply

not_eligible_explanations.household_monthly_take_home: Healthy Start through Universal Credit needs family take-home pay from work of £408 a month or less.

rules.title: Tax-Free Childcare
rules.summary: For every £8 you pay into the account, the government adds £2. Up to £2,000 a year per child.
how_to_claim: Apply at gov.uk/apply-for-tax-free-childcare

not_eligible_explanations.benefits_received: You can't use Tax-Free Childcare at the same time as Universal Credit. UC childcare (up to 85%) is usually better; I can compare both.

rules.notes: UC exclusion is a well-known rule but was NOT confirmed on the fetched page; verify.

rules.title: Help to Save
rules.summary: Save £1-£50 a month and get a 50% bonus from the government.

value.bonus: 50p per £1 saved, paid at year 2 and year 4

how_to_claim: Apply at gov.uk/get-help-savings-low-income
rules.forecast_hook: Use the forecast to pick a monthly amount that never pushes the balance below a safety buffer.
rules.notes: Exact UC earnings threshold not shown on fetched page; capped at likely_eligible.

rules.title: Free prescriptions, dental and glasses (NHS help with health costs)
rules.summary: Some benefits give you full help automatically. Otherwise the NHS Low Income Scheme can help if savings are under £16,000.
rules.transaction_signal: Payments to pharmacies or dentists while on UC/Pension Credit → user may be paying for something free.
how_to_claim: If on a qualifying benefit, show proof at the pharmacy or dentist
Otherwise apply for the NHS Low Income Scheme (HC1 form)

rules.title: Cheap broadband and mobile (social tariff)
rules.summary: Broadband and phone deals from £10-£24 a month for people on Universal Credit and some other benefits.
rules.transaction_signal: Recurring broadband/mobile payment > £25/month → estimated saving = current - cheapest social tariff from same provider.
how_to_claim: Call your current provider and ask for their social tariff; no exit fee to switch within the same provider in most cases

rules.title: Crisis and Resilience Fund (council emergency help)
rules.summary: Council fund (April 2026 to March 2029) for emergencies: food, energy, rent shortfalls. Replaced the Household Support Fund.
rules.trigger_from_forecast: Forecast shows balance < 0 before next income, OR essential bill (rent/energy) at risk.
how_to_claim: Apply on your council's website; rules differ by council

rules.title: Opt-in opportunities for under-represented groups
rules.summary: Some universities, charities and employers lawfully run scholarships, bursaries, grants and mentoring for under-represented groups (Equality Act 2010 positive action, ss.158-159). These are NOT government benefits.
rules.catalogue: data/opportunities.json (TO BUILD: each entry must have a real source_url and a verified date; do not invent programmes)
agent_rules: Never say a state benefit pays more because of ethnicity, religion or sexual orientation: none do, and it would be unlawful.
Only ask about ethnicity after explaining it's optional and only used for opt-in opportunities.
User can delete this fact at any time.

refer_out.to: Citizens Advice or an OISC-registered adviser
Citizens Advice, Shelter (housing), or a solicitor
Council Crisis and Resilience Fund + local food bank
